sources.title: Biographical record and editorial note confirming departure on 30 June 2025
sources.findings: Read Bundestag current biographical record and editorial departure note. Birth is 15 December 1980 in Hanover. Editorial note states resignation submitted 15 June 2025 and membership ended with 30 June 2025; this overrides the stale self-reported line saying member since 2013 to today. Hamburg qualification is Vordiplom, London is LL.M.; doctoral project explicitly unfinished. Personal family and religious details are not reproduced.

sources.title: Archived 19th electoral-term biography: education, party leadership and climate-policy role
sources.findings: Read the archived 19th-term Bundestag biography. It identifies London studies in 2004–2005, party leadership from 27 January 2018, Bundestag membership from October 2013 and climate-policy spokesperson role in 2013–2017. Treat the page as historical and member-supplied, not a current appointment record. Current page lists doctoral admission in 2008 while archive describes research in 2009–2013; no exact doctoral start date is asserted.

sources.title: Current faculty profile: professor of professional practice and MPA faculty co-director
sources.findings: Read Columbia SIPA current faculty profile. It confirms Professor of Professional Practice and Faculty Co-Director, MPA in Global Leadership. Its erroneous ministerial dates December 2001–May 2005 are rejected against the Foreign Office and UN records. Its historical presidency language does not establish current UN office. Do not infer tenure status, a completed PhD, or sole personal authorship of government policies from the title or promotional biography.

sources.title: 25 August 2026: faculty appointments for 2026–27
sources.findings: Read Columbia faculty announcement, explicitly posted 25 August 2026. Baerbock joins in autumn as professor of professional practice and MPA faculty co-director; announcement date is not first working or teaching day. Its description of the UN presidency as already past is not used to shorten her term. The neighbouring biographies and degrees belong to other appointees.

sources.title: 10 September 2025: election on 2 June and eightieth-session presidency
sources.findings: Read UN press release hosted by the UN in India, dated 10 September 2025. It confirms election on 2 June 2025, September 2025–September 2026 session, German foreign-minister service December 2021–May 2025 and parliamentary service through June 2025. Its loose Hamburg undergraduate-degree wording is not converted into a bachelor’s degree: the Bundestag specifies Vordiplom. Election and session opening are separate.

sources.title: Indexed primary-source extract: secretary-general selection process and 8 September 2026 handover
sources.findings: Read explicit indexed primary-source extracts of the 81st General Assembly secretary-general selection page: Baerbock conducted the process until 8 September 2026 and a town hall was held on 23 July. Direct page access returned 403. The exact handover date is therefore labelled as indexed evidence in the dossier, corroborated by indexed 80th-session records and later biographies describing her as former president. No full-page read is claimed.

sources.title: 8 December 2021: Germany’s first female foreign minister takes office
sources.findings: Read Foreign Office report dated 8 December 2021 stating the actual handover from Heiko Maas and Germany’s first female foreign minister taking office. This corrects Columbia’s historical date typo. Future travel plans in the article are not presented as already completed visits.

sources.title: 1 March 2023: presentation of feminist foreign policy guidelines
sources.findings: Read Foreign Office speech presenting feminist foreign policy guidelines on 1 March 2023. Rights, representation and resources are policy priorities, not independently verified outcomes. The speech credits ministry colleagues and distinguishes the Development Ministry’s policy presented with Svenja Schulze. Numerical forecasts and claims about peace-agreement survival are not reproduced as validated findings.

sources.title: 1 March 2023: feminist foreign and development policies and criticism
sources.findings: Read ARD Tagesschau policy explanation and criticism passages. Kristina Lunz of the Centre for Feminist Foreign Policy supported a new approach but questioned consistency with rearmament and demanded matching investment in human security. This is attributed criticism, not an adjudicated finding. Separate foreign-policy guidelines from Schulze’s development policy; do not adopt the article’s quoted court-history claim without independent verification.

sources.title: 2026: candidate dialogues, town hall and secretary-general appointment procedure
sources.findings: Read IISD SDG Knowledge Hub account of candidate dialogues and the completed 23 July 2026 town hall. It explains that the Assembly appoints the Secretary-General on Security Council recommendation. The president’s convening role is distinct from personal power to appoint or from herself holding the Secretary-General office. Future events and candidate status at the article’s earlier cutoff are not carried forward as November facts.

sources.publisher: Center for International Relations and Sustainable Development
sources.title: 7 October 2026: retrospective account of Columbia discussion with Vuk Jeremić
sources.findings: Read CIRSD account dated 7 October 2026, describing a completed Columbia discussion with Vuk Jeremić. This is retrospective evidence of participation, not an advance event listing. The exact discussion date is not separately stated; October 7 is treated as report date. His former candidacy is not Baerbock’s.

sources.title: Indexed retrospective: 26 October 2026 Hammarskjöld Lecture and medal
sources.findings: Read the explicit search-indexed Columbia retrospective stating that she delivered the annual Dag Hammarskjöld Lecture at Uppsala on 26 October 2026 and received its medal. Direct article opens were inaccessible, so both public text and review disclose indexed-only access. The Uppsala university advance press release independently names the event and organisers but does not itself prove attendance. Do not confuse this university/foundation lecture medal with the UN peacekeeping medal or Hammarskjöld’s Nobel award.

sources.title: 27 January 2018: Baerbock and Habeck elected as Green Party co-leaders
sources.findings: Read SRF report of 27 January 2018 confirming that the party congress elected both Annalena Baerbock and Robert Habeck. Preserve joint leadership and do not imply that the party position itself was a federal government office. Service through 2022 is separately supported by Bundestag and UN records.
